source:
Realistic Wheelie Game Prompt

Create a realistic 3D wheelie game inspired by Wheelie Life and Wheelie Challenge with high-quality physics, smooth controls, and realistic bike handling.

Gameplay

- Realistic wheelie balancing using throttle, rear brake, and body lean.
- Physics-based suspension and tire grip.
- Manual, stoppie, and combo trick system.
- First-person and third-person cameras.
- Day/night cycle and weather options.
- Online multiplayer with free roam and wheelie competitions.
- XP progression, achievements, and leaderboards.

Bikes

Include realistic licensed-inspired models (without using trademarks directly) based on popular bikes such as:

- Surron Light Bee X
- Talaria Sting MX5
- E Ride Pro SS
- Rawrr Mantis
- Arctic Leopard
- Yamaha YZ125
- Yamaha YZ250F
- Yamaha YZ450F
- Honda CRF250R
- Honda CRF450R
- KTM 125 SX
- KTM 250 SX-F
- KTM 450 SX-F
- Kawasaki KX250
- Kawasaki KX450
- Suzuki RM-Z250
- Suzuki RM-Z450
- GasGas MC series
- Husqvarna FC series
- Mountain bikes
- BMX bikes
- Road bikes
- Dirt jump bikes

Each bike should have:

- Unique power curve
- Weight
- Wheelbase
- Suspension tuning
- Top speed
- Wheelie balance point
- Upgrade system

Customization

- Plastics
- Graphics kits
- Number plates
- Wheels
- Handlebars
- Seats
- Exhausts
- Motors
- Batteries
- Controllers
- Sprockets
- Tires
- Rider helmets
- Riding gear
- Gloves
- Boots
- Bike stance adjustment

Maps

- Large city
- Highway
- Industrial area
- Country roads
- Dirt tracks
- Skatepark
- Parking lots
- Mountain roads
- Beach boardwalk
- Forest trails

Realistic Effects

- Rear tire smoke
- Dust
- Dirt spray
- Sparks from tail scraping
- Metal scraping sounds
- Tail scrape score multiplier
- Wheel sparks when landing
- Burnouts
- Suspension compression
- Engine vibration
- Dynamic lighting
- Motion blur
- Rain reflections

Tail Scraping

When the rider balances too high:

- The rear fender or scrape bar contacts the ground.
- Generate realistic sparks.
- Play metal scraping audio.
- Leave temporary scrape marks.
- Award style points while maintaining control.
- Increase combo multiplier while scraping.

Crash System

- Physics ragdoll.
- Rider separation from bike.
- Bike damage.
- Scratches and broken plastics.
- Slow-motion crashes.
- Replay camera.

Looping Respawn

When the player crashes:

- Fade to black for less than one second.
- Instantly respawn at the last checkpoint.
- Preserve bike customization.
- Reset physics cleanly.
- Restart in a seamless gameplay loop with no loading screens.
- Option for instant retry during challenge modes.

Controls

Mobile:

- Left thumb joystick
- Throttle
- Front brake
- Rear brake
- Lean forward
- Lean backward
- Clutch
- Gear shifting
- Camera switch

Controller:

- Analog throttle
- Analog brakes
- Manual clutch
- Full vibration feedback

Audio

- Realistic engine sounds for every bike.
- Electric motor whine for e-bikes.
- Tire noise.
- Wind effects.
- Tail scrape grinding.
- Crash sounds.
- Environmental ambience.

Graphics

- Unreal Engine 5 quality visuals.
- Lumen lighting.
- Nanite assets.
- HDR.
- 60-120 FPS support.
- High-quality reflections.
- Detailed rider animations.
- Realistic wheel deformation under load.

Game Modes

- Free Ride
- Wheelie Challenge
- Longest Wheelie
- Online Multiplayer
- Drift Mode
- Time Trial
- Skill Challenges
- Freestyle Sessions

AI Riders

- Dynamic difficulty.
- Competitive races.
- Wheelie battles.
- Realistic mistakes and recoveries.

Overall goal: create the most realistic and polished wheelie game possible, with advanced physics, immersive visuals, responsive controls, extensive bike customization, satisfying tail-scraping mechanics with sparks and sound effects, and an instant looping respawn system that keeps gameplay fast and continuous.

image_prompt.text: Rideable-width roads threading the whole map - multi-lane highway, city streets, winding country and mountain roads with guardrails, and dirt trails
A large open shared area the whole server uses at once, held here as a common free-roam ground rather than an extraction field
Skatepark ramps, quarter pipes, rails, and knock-around street props whose physics reactions are the entertainment
A sprawling city district with streets, intersections, traffic lights, streetlights, signs, and parked vehicles
An industrial area of warehouses, loading docks, and open parking lots
A beach boardwalk running along the water
Forest trails and dirt tracks with uneven ground

layout_placement.text: Checkpoints across the map that a crashed rider is instantly restored to with position, orientation, and zeroed velocity, preserving bike customization

notes: Simulation is dominant: free roam with no lap and no finish is Vehicle Sim by the Racing boundary note. Racing contributes checkpoint-respawn only, for the stated instant-respawn loop.

The prompt lists ten named environments under a 'Maps' heading. Whether that is one contiguous open world or ten separate maps is unresolved; ten separate maps would force P4. Built here as one world.
The preset's shared resource field has no function in a wheelie game - kept and labelled rather than dropped, per intake policy.
Unreal Engine 5, Lumen, Nanite, and HDR are not available on this platform; treat as a fidelity intent, not a spec.

open_questions.ask: Is this one connected open world you can ride between all ten areas in, or ten separate maps you pick from a menu?
How far across should the city be - a few blocks, or a full drivable metro?

theme: Photoreal modern urban and rural - asphalt, concrete, guardrails, dust and dirt, wet reflective surfaces at night

coverage_missing.ask: One connected world, or ten separate maps?
How large is the city relative to the rest?
Which mode is the map built around - free roam, longest-wheelie scoring, or racing AI riders? They want different road layouts.

answers.ask: Is this one connected open world you can ride between all ten areas in, or ten separate maps you pick from a menu?
answers.answer: Use ten separate maps selected from a menu, so each area can be focused and run smoothly while supporting its intended riding style.

answers.ask: How far across should the city be - a few blocks, or a full drivable metro?
answers.answer: Make the city a compact few-block urban map with connected streets, intersections, and riding spots rather than a full metro.
